findings.title: Failure ledger is not required to preserve the trace cause set, primary cause or chronology
findings.expected: Immutable SPEC0235 lines418–423 requires an ordered failures.json preserving chronological primary and additional causes; lines397–409 requires rejecting contradictory evidence bindings. R3 review contract explicitly requires actual status/failure/record bindings.

code.detail: Terminal status is checked from the supplied ledger, but many distinct priority1 cause sets have the same INFRA_FAILURE outcome.
For each supplied ledger entry, validates its referenced FAILURE record only. No reverse coverage requirement, unique-reference requirement or ordered/consecutive order requirement.
Reached-proof validation runs for all statuses, but the one-way failure relation still permits contradictory failure ledgers.

findings.reproducer: Run the real frozen controller with a wholly simulated peer that emits forbidden auth then refuses cleanup. Its actual report is INFRA_FAILURE/exit1; original failures.json contains PRIVACY order0 followed by four CLEANUP causes, with unchanged matching HOST FAILURE events. Clone only the report/retained map and replace/re-hash the failures artifact three ways: remove PRIVACY, reverse the five causes, or duplicate PRIVACY. assertEvidenceBindings accepts all three mutated artifact sets unchanged. Original artifact set is also confirmed valid first.
findings.impact: The artifact verifier can accept a cause ledger that loses the primary privacy violation, invents a duplicate or reverses chronology while its retained trusted trace contradicts it. The process still reports failure; this is an audit/evidence-integrity contract defect, not a demonstrated native escape, automatic positive-status bypass or evidence that the controller normally omits its causes.
findings.safeCorrection: Require an exact ordered correspondence between the complete retained HOST FAILURE record set and failures.json: each reachable cause represented once, correct artifactRef and fields, consecutive unique order in canonical chronology, primary cause first. Preserve the explicitly defined record-cap/null-reference case rather than requiring nonexistent future records. Add the three counterexamples as rejects. No correction was made by this reviewer.
